stories.body: Taiwanese voters went to the polls Saturday to choose mayors, council members and other officials across 22 cities and counties. In Taipei, incumbent Mayor Chiang Wan-an of the opposition Kuomintang faced Puma Shen of the governing Democratic Progressive Party in a race Chiang called close. Housing, transport and childcare featured in the campaigns. Taiwanese officials also warned of suspected Chinese interference and disinformation, allegations Beijing denied.
stories.headline: Taiwan votes in local elections as Beijing faces accusations of interference

stories.body: Ukraine shared a proposed Black Sea ceasefire with international allies to allow food exports to continue and was awaiting a response from Moscow, a senior Ukrainian official said Friday. The announcement came a day after Ukrainian authorities said Russia attacked two foreign grain carriers near the port of Odesa.
stories.headline: Ukraine proposes a Black Sea ceasefire to protect food exports

stories.body: Doctors Without Borders said an Israeli strike directly hit one of its Gaza City clinics on Friday, killing two staff members who worked as guards. The organization said the clinic was clearly marked and it had shared the location with the Israeli military. The military alleged without providing evidence that the two men were members of Hamas. Doctors Without Borders said the deaths brought the number of its staff killed in Gaza to 17.
stories.headline: Israeli strike on a Gaza City clinic kills two Doctors Without Borders staff

stories.body: Pakistan and Turkey renewed their pledge to defend Saudi Arabia at talks in Islamabad on Friday under a three-country pact that treats an armed attack on one member as an attack on all three. The governments condemned Houthi attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. Cross-border attacks have increased since an informal ceasefire in Yemen broke down in July. An October strike on Riyadh’s international airport killed 13 people and injured more than 300, the BBC reported.
stories.headline: Pakistan and Turkey reaffirm support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks

stories.body: Venezuela’s National Assembly chief, Jorge Rodríguez, announced plans to repeal a 2024 law that bars people who promoted or supported sanctions against the country from holding office. He said the decision followed transition talks between the interim government and parts of the opposition. María Corina Machado, who was barred from running in the 2024 presidential election and returned from exile last month, has been excluded from those talks. The interim government has promised elections and has yet to set a date.
stories.headline: Venezuela plans to repeal a law used to bar opposition figures from office

stories.body: Canada’s Supreme Court ruled 6–1 that Quebec could use the Constitution’s notwithstanding clause to shield most of its secularism law from challenges under the Charter of Rights and Freedoms. The law bars teachers, police officers and some other public-sector workers from wearing religious symbols such as hijabs, turbans and crosses on the job. The ruling has implications beyond Quebec because the clause allows governments to override certain Charter protections for renewable five-year periods.
stories.headline: Canada’s Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec’s ban on religious symbols for some public workers

stories.body: The UK Department for Work and Pensions took online services for Universal Credit, pensions and disability benefits offline as a precaution while it investigated a cyber incident. The department said regular payments would continue and claimants would face no penalties for missing online journal entries during the outage. Some claimants told the BBC that payments they expected had failed to arrive. Downing Street said it had found no evidence that personal data had been lost.
stories.headline: Cyber incident cuts off millions in the UK from online benefits and pension services

stories.body: Norwegian low-cost long-haul carrier Norse Atlantic Airways filed for bankruptcy after rising jet fuel costs squeezed its finances and lessors issued termination notices for all 12 aircraft in its fleet. The company canceled all upcoming flights, including those operated by its UK subsidiary, and told passengers to stay away from airports. With customer service closed, it directed affected passengers to their booking agents, insurers or card issuers.
stories.headline: Norse Atlantic Airways files for bankruptcy and cancels all flights

stories.body: El País’s final forecast gave the People’s Party and Vox an 83% chance of together winning the 176 seats needed for a majority in Spain’s Congress. The campaign closed Friday with PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo in Seville, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Frente Amplio candidate Ada Colau in Madrid, and Vox leader Santiago Abascal in Valencia. The Catalan Socialists are hoping to repeat their 2023 result, when their 19 seats helped keep Sánchez in office.
stories.headline: Spain heads to Sunday’s snap election with the PP and Vox favored to win a majority

stories.body: Rescuers found at least 14 people dead and 84 alive aboard a migrant boat spotted adrift roughly 65 to 70 kilometers off El Hierro in the Canary Islands. Survivors said they had left The Gambia 10 days earlier. Six people in critical condition were evacuated by helicopter, and survivors arriving at La Restinga showed signs of dehydration and hypothermia. Spain deployed 120 military emergency personnel to El Hierro to help treat people arriving on the island.
stories.headline: At least 14 people die aboard a migrant boat off El Hierro

stories.body: Spain’s maritime authorities approved towing the Med Emre to Cartagena after the diesel tanker capsized between Valencia and Ibiza, killing its chief engineer and injuring several crew members. The ship will be towed upside down to the Escombreras basin, which officials said was the only port in the area deep enough and sheltered enough for the weeks of work needed to remove its cargo and fuel. Inspectors found the hull stable and detected a light slick just over a mile long near the wreck.
stories.headline: Capsized diesel tanker is being towed to Cartagena

stories.body: About 9.6 million people receive contributory pensions in Spain, which are set to rise 3.5% in 2027 under a formula tied to average inflation over 12 months. Preliminary figures put annual inflation at 4.1% in November, down from 4.9% in October, with confirmation due December 15. The government also announced increases of 8.8% to 14.2% for minimum and noncontributory pensions and a 14.1% increase in the national minimum income benefit.
stories.headline: Spain’s contributory pensions are set to rise 3.5% in 2027

stories.body: Trains on the R4 commuter line between Sant Vicenç de Calders and Manresa ran more than 50 minutes late on Friday, according to Renfe’s live maps. Renfe and Adif reported an infrastructure fault without specifying where it occurred. Earlier in the week, an overhead power failure forced buses to replace trains between Cerdanyola del Vallès and Montcada-Manresa during the morning rush, and separate problems disrupted service at Arc de Triomf, Sants and Montcada-Bifurcació.
stories.headline: Rodalies R4 delays exceed 50 minutes on fourth straight day of disruptions
